how-to-give-every-kid-equal-playing-time.text:
Youth Lineup Rotator · guide

How to give every kid equal playing time

Fair playing time is arithmetic before it is anything else. Count the spots on the field, multiply by the number of periods, and divide by the roster. What is left over is the bench, and the only fair thing to do with it is share it out.

The numbers for 7v7 soccer, four periods

Seven on the field for four periods is 28 player-periods. This table shows how they split for rosters of 8 to 14, with nobody more than one period ahead of anybody else.

PlayersOn the bench each periodPeriods each child plays
814 play 4, 4 play 3
921 play 4, 8 play 3
1038 play 3, 2 play 2
1146 play 3, 5 play 2
1254 play 3, 8 play 2
1362 play 3, 11 play 2
147everyone plays 2

Three rules that make a rotation feel fair

  1. Spread the bench. Nobody sits two periods in a row if you can help it. A child who sits the second and third period has watched half the game.
  2. Share the goalkeeper job. One period in goal each, assigned to children who are willing, rather than one child in goal for the whole game.
  3. Carry the debt forward. A child who sat out two periods last Saturday should be first in line this Saturday. The planner does this when you paste last game's sat: numbers in.

Do it in seconds

The Youth Lineup Rotator makes the whole sheet, including who comes on and off at each break, and runs entirely in your browser.

Common questions

How many periods should each child play?

Divide the field spots by the roster. In 7v7 with four periods there are 28 player-periods to hand out, so with 11 players everyone plays two or three periods and 6 players get the extra one. Nobody can be exactly equal unless the roster divides the spots evenly, so the fair target is a difference of at most one period.

Is it fair to bench the weakest players more?

Not in most recreational leagues, and many require minimum play. The planner treats every available child the same on time and uses skill only to spread strength across periods, so a strong lineup in one period is not paid for with a weak one in the next.

What about a child who arrives late?

Mark them late: 1 and the planner counts only the periods they are there, then shares the bench turns among the periods that remain. They are not penalised for the missed time.

YOUTH LINEUP ROTATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Youth soccer lineup generator: equal playing time, no kid benched twice in a row

Type your roster and the positions on the field. Get a period-by-period lineup where every child plays about the same, the goalkeeper job is shared, your strongest players are spread across periods, and each substitution is spelled out for the sideline. Free, no sign-up, no app to install.

Wondering how the numbers work out for your team size? Read how to give every kid equal playing time, with a worked example.

1. The game

2. Your players

Pick a format, add your players, then press Make the lineup.

Lineup

Playing time

How it works

Fair time. The planner counts how many periods each child is there for and how many they sit. It then searches thousands of arrangements and keeps the one where bench turns are spread most evenly, counting a child who sat last game as already owed some time on the field.

Rules that always hold. Nobody is in two places in one period, nobody plays while absent, and nobody is put in a position you ruled out. Beyond that it prefers, in order: every position filled, equal time, no one benched twice running, one period at most in goal, a change of position, and balanced strength.

Checked. The test suite validates every lineup against those rules and compares the search with an exhaustive search of every possible lineup on small teams.

Limits. It plans whole periods, not minute-by-minute rotations. It does not know your league's rules, but you can pick a minimum-play rule (half the game, three quarters, every period) and the page flags any child who falls short. Check the rule itself with your league. The skill numbers are only the ones you type.

Common questions

How do I make sure every kid gets equal playing time?

Add the roster and the positions on the field. The planner counts the periods each child is available and spreads the bench turns so that nobody plays more than one period more than anybody else. A child who arrives late or leaves early is only counted for the periods they are there.

Can it stop a kid sitting out two periods in a row?

Yes. Sitting two periods running is penalised far more heavily than any other preference, so the planner avoids it whenever the numbers allow. With a very large roster it can be impossible, and then the page names who sits twice instead of hiding it.

How do I share goalkeeper time?

Leave the keeper limit at one period. Every child allowed in goal then takes at most one period there, and if too few children are allowed the page tells you which ones must repeat.

What if some kids are stronger than others?

Give each child a skill from 1 to 5. With strength balance on, the planner keeps the total skill on the field about the same in every period, so your strongest players are not all on the bench together. Turn it off if you do not rate your players.

How do I keep it fair across the whole season?

After each game press Copy next game's roster. It adds a sat: number for each child who sat. Paste it in next time and those children are first in line to play.

Is my team's information uploaded?

No. Names and ratings stay in your browser. There are no accounts, no ads and no email addresses. A shared setup link carries the roster inside the link itself, so only share it with people on your team.
